 ADVERTISEMENT   Filtered By: Weather Weather Signal No. 2 raised over Batanes, parts of Babuyan Islands due to Super Typhoon Rosal 
 By GMA News Published October 21, 2026 11:51pm 
 + Add GMA on Google Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google. Courtesy: PAGASA Super Typhoon Rosal moved northwestward over the sea east of Extreme Northern Luzon, state weather bureau PAGASA said in its 11 p.m. Wednesday bulletin.
 As of 10 p.m., the center of Rosal was located 645 kilometers east of Calayan, Cagayan, packing maximum sustained winds of 205 kilometers per hour (km/h) and gusts of up to 250 km/h. It was moving northwestward at 20 km/h.
 PAGASA raised Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 2 over Batanes and the northeastern portion of the Babuyan Islands.
 Signal No. 1 was hoisted over the following areas:

 The rest of the Babuyan Islands
 Mainland Cagayan
 Eastern Isabela, including Maconacon, Divilacan, Palanan, Santa Maria, Cabagan, Delfin Albano, Santo Tomas, Tumauini, San Pablo, Ilagan City, San Mariano, and Dinapigue
 Ilocos Norte
 Apayao
 PAGASA said Signal No. 3 may be raised over Batanes during Rosal's passage. However, the likelihood of raising the signal would decrease if the super typhoon follows a more north-northwestward track.
 Residents in parts of Northern Luzon have stepped up preparations as Rosal approached the region, while Malacañang assured the public that government agencies were ready for the storm's possible effects.
 According to Joseph Morong's report on "24 Oras," residents in Batanes reinforced their homes' windows with wooden boards and nails and secured their roofs to withstand strong winds. Similar preparations were undertaken in larger buildings.
 In Laoag City, Ilocos Norte, fishermen in Barangay La Paz temporarily stopped going out to sea due to rough conditions brought by the approaching storm.
 Office of Civil Defense spokesperson Junie Castillo said OCD Regions I and II had been coordinating directly with local government units in their respective areas.
 He added that resources, equipment, food supplies, and non-food items had already been prepositioned in preparation for possible emergencies.
 Rosal is expected to make its closest approach to Extreme Northern Luzon between Thursday afternoon and Friday morning, PAGASA said.
 The super typhoon is forecast to gradually weaken and may be downgraded to a typhoon on Thursday. By Saturday, it is expected to weaken rapidly and may be downgraded to a severe tropical storm.
 Rosal is forecast to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) by Friday evening or early Saturday morning. — VBL, GMA News
